If the Customer or Sponsor misses a review or sign-off (A-04 to A-12), approval may be late, delaying dependent WPs and milestones 1.7.2, 1.2.11, 1.6.3 or 1.6.12.
Mitigate: book each session one week ahead with a fallback date, send the documents at the start of the review lag and allow online attendance or a recorded demo (PR-12).
If WebSocket scaling in 1.3.3 is insufficient, the Nov 12-20 load test (1.5.3) may miss 15,000 users, error rate < 1% or p90 < 200 ms, requiring rework before RC (1.5.8).

Mitigate: build the service on Socket.IO with its PostgreSQL adapter, so that a WebSocket server can be added without code changes, and test 1,000 connections on staging in 1.3.5, one week before the full load test.
If development in 1.3/1.4 exceeds its hours (up to +40%, Medium-Low estimate confidence), 1.4.8 (Dec 7) may slip, reducing Could-have scope or time for testing.
Mitigate: build the Must-have functions first, compare logged and remaining hours every week and, if a package is late, cut the Could-have functions FR-05, FR-10 and FR-13 first (Charter).
If the Customer changes requirements after SRS sign-off (1.1.8, Sep 18), design and development rework may increase cost and delay delivery.

Mitigate: every request goes through change control (1.7.5) with an impact analysis; the PM approves changes of up to 2% of the budget (15,140,000 VND) and up to 3 days, the Sponsor approves larger ones.
If store review exceeds 3 working days or rejects a build (A-13), publication may miss Jan 15, 2027 and delay 1.6.12.
Mitigate: check the release builds against the App Store Review Guidelines and Google Play policies, and complete the store listings, privacy details and in-app purchase products before submission.
If cloud/CDN activation exceeds 2 working days after purchase (A-14), setup (1.2.7, Oct 13-20) may start late, delaying 1.3.2 and the MVP.
Mitigate: get the activation time in writing before buying (1.7.3) and start 1.2.7 with the parts that need no cloud account, so that only the staging and CDN setup waits.
If streaming traffic exceeds 5,000 GB/month (PR-04), CDN overage may increase the cost of 1.2.7.

Accept with a contingency reserve: pay the traffic above 5 TB from the 1.2.7 contingency (12,292,906 VND, about 22 TB at 550 VND/GB including VAT); keep 128 kbps as the default audio quality to limit traffic.
If ZAP or ASVS/MASVS checks in 1.5.3 (Nov 12-20) find a critical/high vulnerability, fixes may exceed the 5 days in 1.5.4, delaying RC and failing NFR-05.
Mitigate: check the security items of the code review checklist in every pull request and run an OWASP ZAP baseline scan on staging in 1.3.5, one week before 1.5.3.

If the handling of account and listening data does not meet the Vietnamese Law on Personal Data Protection (effective Jan 1, 2026), the Customer may refuse acceptance (1.6.3) or a store may reject the apps, leading to rework of the account functions.

Avoid: turn the legal duties into checkable items (consent at registration, privacy notice in Vietnamese and English, in-app account and data deletion (FR-02), listening data used only for FR-08) and check them in the design review (1.2.8).
If a member is absent for > 3 working days, their singly owned WPs may stop and delay dependent milestones.
Mitigate: name a backup person for every work package (Team Charter) and keep the code, documents and Jira tasks updated every day, so that the backup can take over within 1 working day.
If Flutter misses device targets (cold < 2 s, warm < 1 s, battery < 6%/h; NFR-03/04), rework after 1.5.3 may delay RC (1.5.8).
Mitigate: measure the launch time and battery use on the slowest devices (Samsung Galaxy A07, iPhone 11) in 1.3.5, one week before 1.5.3, and fix the gaps before the device tests.
If the restore drill before go-live (1.6.4) exceeds RTO 4 h or RPO 24 h (NFR-10), production deployment may be postponed, delaying 1.6.12.
Mitigate: use the daily automated backup of the managed PostgreSQL package (PR-02) and write and rehearse the restore steps in the operations guide (1.6.9) before the drill.
If backend/API decisions or code reviews wait more than 1 working day for the Technical Lead, dependent development may stop, delaying 1.3.8 or 1.4.8.
Mitigate: use the shared API contract (1.2.6), identify review cover in 1.7.1 and check individual workload in 1.7.4/1.7.5.
If a developer lacks the skills required by an assigned package, code may fail acceptance or introduce repeated defects, increasing rework and delaying the release candidate (1.5.8).
Mitigate: check skills before assignment; review code and developer unit tests within the development WP; check integration in 1.3.5/1.4.5.
